title: Did China Play Jensen Huang?
gist: Palmer's China Brief probes whether Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese asset Alice Huang of Megaspeed (Nvidia's largest Southeast Asian chip customer) was a honey trap or an 'intelligence entrepreneur' play, notes the White House ignored warnings while approving H200 exports to China, and predicts tougher chip restrictions from the new Congress; it also covers China's marriage registrations at an 18-year low, a two-month trade-truce extension to Jan. 10, 2027, and a 20% cut in China-Japan flight seats.

themes.theme: Huang-Megaspeed scandal: facts and red flags

insights.claim: After Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials believe worked for Beijing, Nvidia stock dropped and the company launched an investigation.

insights.claim: Alice Huang became controlling shareholder of Megaspeed — a Singapore-based, China-linked cloud firm that is Nvidia's largest chip customer in Southeast Asia — in 2023, shortly after the Biden administration imposed sweeping chip restrictions on China.

insights.so_what: Timing suggests Megaspeed as a post-sanctions conduit; Nvidia's Southeast Asia revenue quality is in question.

themes.theme: Trade truce extension and APEC Shenzhen

insights.claim: The U.S.-China trade truce was formally extended by two months through Jan. 10, 2027, leaving room for Xi and Trump to sign a more permanent deal at the APEC summit in Shenzhen.
insights.speaker: James Palmer
insights.so_what: Tariff snapback risk is deferred to Jan. 10, 2027 — a key date for trade-sensitive positions.

insights.claim: Xi knows Trump needs a victory and is likely to come out ahead in any agreement, but domestic U.S. political pressure, especially after the Huang case, could blow up a deal before it is in place.
